Tsebrykove Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tsebrykove, Ukraine

Demolished. Little is documented about this cemetery, though it appears on a 1941 Russian topographic map, presumably demolished during WWII or shortly after; locals still remember the site as a former Jewish cemetery. Little is known of Tsebrykove's Jewish community, named 'Hoffnung' until 1900; 25 Jewish families lived and worked in the nearby Freyberg colony (later absorbed into Tsebrykove in the 1930s) during the 1920s-30s, and a Jewish primary school operated until the mid-1930s. Population reached 210 (7%) by 1939. Nazi occupation from August 8, 1941 murdered 185 regional Jews that same month.
